name: Real estate appraiser

pf.license.need: Each appraiser holds their own state appraiser license or certification at the right level (trainee, licensed, certified residential, certified general). A trainee works under a supervising appraiser who inspects with them and signs the report. A property type above the appraiser's level (multi-unit, land, commercial) is booked only with someone certified for it, where the state's form says so.
pf.license.ask: Each appraiser's license or certification number, type and level. The company's registration number, where the state's form asks for one.
pf.license.who_holds: Each appraiser holds their own license. The company holds its own registration where the state asks. Only the appraiser who did the work signs the report.
pf.license.check: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, insurance or registration (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
pf.license.blocks_live: Where the state licenses appraisers: no appraisal is offered until the company's and the appraiser's numbers check out. A property type above the appraiser's level is offered only with someone certified for it.
pf.license.insurance_bond: Errors-and-omissions insurance where the state's form requires it. Shown as given by the business, not checked by Rosie.
pf.license.background_checks: Only where the state's rules require them, or as the business's own word.
pf.license.shown_to_customers: The appraiser's license number on the engagement letter, offers, confirmations and the report, where the state's rules require it.
pf.license.not_this_work: Home inspections, repairs, real estate sales or listings, and a mortgage appraisal ordered by a borrower (the lender orders those). A value is never promised, set in advance or 'hit'.

pf.services.pattern: Set service: one appraisal visit at the property, priced by the property's size and type, with a signed report later.

list.name: Home appraisal
list.price_kind: set by the customer's answers (square feet, house or condo, acreage)
list.example: house up to 2,500 sq ft: $550; 2,501 to 4,000 sq ft: $700; condo or townhouse: $450 (the example business's own prices)
list.length: about 1 hour on site: every level measured and photographed; the signed report follows in about 5 business days
list.where: at the property; an adult lets the appraiser in, or a lockbox set up by the agent for an empty home
list.money: card saved at booking; charged at DONE

list.name: Condo or townhouse appraisal
list.money: card saved at booking; charged at DONE

list.name: Land appraisal (the second kind of work)
list.price_kind: quoted from the parcel's details and photos first
list.example: a vacant lot: $500, with a certified appraiser

list.name: Large property evaluation
list.price_kind: set by the appraiser at the visit from the size; only the $89 trip fee is promised before
list.example: acreage with several buildings: priced on site; the fee never depends on the value found

list.name: 4-unit building appraisal (2 to 4 units)
list.price_kind: quoted from the listing, the rent roll and photos first
list.example: a 4-unit building: $640, with a deposit; Sam OKs any quote over $500; needs a certified appraiser

list.name: Appraisal update
list.example: $150, about 30 minutes: an update of a recent appraisal after repairs or a change
list.money: booked like the first appraisal, with its own engagement letter; paid in full when booking (the example business's setting)

list.name: Rent analysis
list.example: $199 (market rent for a rental or an in-law unit); $249 when Sam does it himself
list.where: done from the visit's notes and market data

list.name: Second value date
list.price_kind: one price, an add-on at the visit
list.example: $160: a second value for another date, like a date of death and today

list.name: Trip fee
list.example: $89: only for a late cancel or no way in that Sam confirms, or a return visit when part of the property could not be entered

list.name: Value consult and report checks (at Lee Valuation Office)
list.example: 30-minute value consult $35; sales summary $20; appraisal report check $40; second look at another appraiser's report $55; estate valuation planning meeting, about 2½ hours, $140; at the property $75 (the example office's own prices)
list.where: at the office, by video, or at the property
list.money: card saved for the $20 fee; paid at the office after

pf.services.start_times: Set starts, like 8:00am and 1:00pm. The wrap-up time is told at booking.
pf.services.notice: 2 days' notice by default, so access can be set up. A sooner time only if Sam says yes.
pf.services.capacity: One appraiser per appraisal. A property type above the appraiser's level only with someone certified.
pf.services.nobody_home: Sometimes: an empty home is entered with a lockbox code the agent or owner set up. An occupied home needs an adult (the owner, a tenant or the agent) to let the appraiser in.
pf.services.online: Value consults and report checks can be done by video.
pf.services.not_offered: A mortgage appraisal ordered by a borrower, home inspections, repairs, listings or sales, and any promise of a value.
pf.services.partner_work: None. Rosie never names or refers another business.

About how many square feet, and the year built

The value date: today, or a past date like a date of death
Is a lender asking for it? (A lender orders its own appraisal.)
Is the home lived in or empty?
after_a_time: Pets at the house, and where they'll be
Additions or remodels since it was built
Who will let the appraiser in: you, a tenant or an agent
Will you meet the appraiser at the start?
secure_page_only: The agent's or tenant's mobile, and the access link they fill in
The lockbox or door code, typed only by whoever sets up access
Deeds, earlier appraisals, leases and lists of improvements
pf.questions.who_may_book: An adult who owns the property or acts for the owner: an executor, a trustee, an attorney or an agent. A tenant books only with the owner's yes. Nobody books a mortgage appraisal that a lender will rely on: the lender orders those. Nobody under 18 books or signs.

words: a ceiling or floor giving way right now
what_happens: A gas smell, sparks, smoke or a carbon monoxide alarm: whoever is there gets out first, then calls 911 and the gas company from outside. No booking until the home is safe.
A ceiling or floor giving way right now: everyone gets out and stays out, then calls 911. No booking until the fire department or the building department says it is safe to go in.

Live wires hanging down or flooding up to the outlets: stay away from that area, and call 911 if anyone is in danger. The appraisal can be booked for the rest of the property; the appraiser will not enter that area, and the report says so.
pf.safety.booking_goes_on: No, for gas, sparks, smoke, a carbon monoxide alarm or a ceiling or floor giving way. Yes, with the unsafe area left out, for live wires or flooding.

pf.first_steps.agreement: The business's own engagement letter, signed on the secure page before the time is booked: who the client is, what the appraisal is for, who may rely on it, the value date, and that the fee does not depend on the value. Rosie never writes or edits it.
pf.first_steps.access: Access set up by whoever controls the property: the owner or occupant, a tenant, or an agent with the listing agent, on a link the client forwards. Due by 5pm the day before.
pf.first_steps.documents: Deeds, earlier appraisals, leases, permits and a list of improvements, added on the secure page if there are any.
prep_for_reminder: Every room, closet, attic and garage reachable, with the utilities on
Pets out of the house, or put away
A list of improvements since it was built, with dates, if you have one
Leases and rent amounts for any rented unit

pf.visit.check_in: The owner or occupant, or the agent, lets the appraiser in. For an empty home the appraiser uses the lockbox and DONE confirms the visit. A client who meets the appraiser gives the code at the door, or at the wrap-up.
pf.visit.entry_codes: The lockbox code is shown only to the appraiser, only on the day, and each view is logged.
pf.visit.what_is_checked: Every level measured and photographed, inside and out; the condition, layout and updates noted. Anything that can't be entered is listed in the report.
pf.visit.not_examined: A room or building that can't be entered is listed as not entered. A return visit is offered for the trip fee, with the client's OK.
pf.visit.walk_through: A short wrap-up: what happens next. The value is never given at the visit; it is in the report only.
pf.visit.changes_at_visit: An add-on (a rent analysis, a second value date) only if the client says yes first, priced before it is done. The fee never depends on the value found, the loan or the sale closing.
pf.visit.proof_done: DONE from the appraiser's phone, with photos. The signed report follows by the date promised.
pf.visit.report: A signed appraisal report sent on a secure link by the date promised at booking (the example: 5 business days). A later date is told to the client before the old one passes. Rosie tracks the date.
pf.visit.report_release: Sam picks per service: the report goes out at once, or once the bill is paid. Where the state's rules forbid holding a report, it goes out at once.

pf.money.start: Appraisals: a card saved at booking, charged at DONE. Consults and report checks at the office: a card saved for the fee, paid at the office after.
pf.money.other_ways: Nothing taken and the bill texted after; paid in full when booking (an appraisal update); a deposit and the rest on the bill for a multi-unit building quoted first.
pf.money.deposits: None by default on a set-price appraisal. A multi-unit or land assignment quoted from details may take a deposit; the cap, if any, comes from the state form.
pf.money.fees: Late cancel, or no way in at the start time: the business's own trip fee (the example: $89). A return visit when part of the property could not be entered: the trip fee. Sam confirms each one; no answer, no fee.
pf.money.fee_rule: The fee never depends on the value found, on the loan or on the sale closing. A fee tied to a set value is never accepted.
pf.money.tax: A sales tax line only where the state taxes appraisal services, from the state form.
pf.money.rosfield_fee: The usual $2 per confirmed booking. Whether a rule against paying for appraisal assignments reaches Rosfield's $2 is a question for counsel before launch.

never_in_texts: The street address in a first text to someone new
The value or any part of the report: only the secure link
Why the appraisal is wanted (an estate, a divorce): only the secure page
pf.messages.who_gets_texts: The client. The agent or tenant who sets up access only after their own yes on the access page.
pf.messages.minors: Nobody under 18 books or signs the engagement letter.

skills: Value consults and report checks at the office
pf.staff.licenses: Each appraiser's own license or certification at the level the property needs, where the state licenses appraisers.
pf.staff.stand_in: Another appraiser with the same level and skills may stand in, with the client's OK first.
pf.staff.supervision: A trainee appraises only with a supervising appraiser who inspects with them and signs, where the state's rules allow trainees.
pf.staff.who_oks: Sam OKs quotes over $500 and every fee. Pat, the office manager, may too; Sam's answer wins.

pf.rules.independence: Nobody may ask the appraiser to reach a value. A request for a set value, or a fee tied to the value, is declined and told to Sam.
pf.rules.agreement: A signed engagement letter before the appraisal starts, naming the client, the intended use and the intended users, where the state's rules require it.
pf.rules.report_deadline: The report reaches the client by the date promised at booking. A later date is told to the client before the old one passes. Rosie tracks the date.
pf.rules.fee_independence: The fee can't depend on the value found, the loan or the sale closing.
pf.rules.who_relies: Only the client and the users named in the letter may rely on the report. Anyone else needs the client's OK.
pf.rules.license_shown: The license number on offers, confirmations and the report, where the state's rules require it.
pf.rules.records: 5 years, or longer where the state's rules ask: the letter, the report, the photos and the notes.

matter_most: A borrower asks for an appraisal to give a lender: Rosie says the lender orders its own, and nothing is booked.
The client asks the appraiser to reach a set value: declined; the booking stays only for a fair appraisal, and Sam is told.
The sale or loan falls through: an ordinary cancel, judged only by the notice given.
Access isn't set up by 5pm the day before: Sam is asked to call, and the client is told. The booking stays.
The lockbox code doesn't work: the appraiser texts it, the client and the access person get a link for a new code, and the visit moves.
Part of the property can't be entered: it is listed in the report, and a return visit is offered for the trip fee.
The report runs late: the client hears the new date before the old one passes.
The client wants the value changed after the report: the value is the appraiser's own; a factual mistake goes to Sam.
A moved appraisal carries the signed letter and the access link to the new date.
pf.edges.rest: All other edge cases are handled the generic way.

notes:
Kept words: 'Trip fee' (the $89 fee for a late cancel or no way in, the parent's word too), 'Grace' (the master's grace time), 'leak' and 'color' (the master's shared safety and fairness lines, S13-40 lists color among protected traits).
New profession on the REDESIGN 2 master (batch S1, Tue Oct 27 2026), started from the refitted inspector overlay (set 'from'): an appraisal runs like an inspection (a signed engagement letter before booking, access set up by whoever controls the property, a short wrap-up at the end, a signed report later), so the inspector is the right parent. The walk-through became a wrap-up: the appraiser never gives the value at the visit.
Flow B is the usual side: Lee Appraisal (home, condo and multi-unit appraisals, with land appraisals as the second kind of work, for certified appraisers). Flow A is Lee Valuation Office, Sam's office: a 30-minute value consult, report checks and an estate valuation planning meeting, at the office, by video or at the property.
Prices are the example business's own: home appraisal $550 (house up to 2,500 sq ft), condo $450, land appraisal $500, appraisal update $150 (paid in full), rent analysis $199 ($249 when Sam does it), second value date $160, a multi-unit building quoted from the listing and rent roll at $640 (Sam OKs over $500), trip fee $89. Flow A: value consult $35, sales summary $20, appraisal report check $40, second look at a report $55, estate valuation planning meeting $140, at the property $75.
Money, flow B: main list|card|card (a card saved at booking, charged at DONE), list|none|bill (the bill after; the report goes out once it is paid), list|full|none (an appraisal update paid in full), photos|deposit|bill (a multi-unit building quoted first: $160 deposit, $480 on the bill). Flow A: list|card|counter (main), list|none|counter, list|full|none, list|card|card. No visit-priced path and no tied-to-value fee: the fee never depends on the value found, the loan or the sale.
Who must not be booked (pf.questions, pf.edges): a borrower who wants an appraisal to give a lender (the lender orders those; nothing is booked); anyone asking for a set value; a tenant without the owner's yes; anyone under 18. These are Rosie's own conduct: what it books and says; what people do off Rosie is not ours.
Danger words (pf.safety): a gas smell, sparks or smoke, a carbon monoxide alarm (no booking until safe); a ceiling or floor giving way right now (no booking until it is safe); live wires hanging down, flooding up to the outlets (booking goes on, that area left out). The danger-first call (B3-11, B3-18) uses water up to the outlets, so the two steps read as one conversation.
Settings: arrive a set start (8:00am and 1:00pm), cutoff 6pm the day before; booking choices limited to a set time. Nothing is sent now: S2-30's Yes branch and every sent-now branch are off.
Rename pairs: only the inspector's pairs that match the frozen master were kept and re-worded for appraisal; addresses and license numbers are made up (EX-1042 style). The master's 'Leak repair' sign-up row reads 'Large property evaluation' (priced at the visit by size).
Own steps (same ids as the parent): B6-x01 (Alex gets a link to forward to whoever lets the appraiser in) and B7-x02 (the access is set up on the link).
For the verifier: the lockbox and the agent's access are the parent's design, kept because many private appraisals are of empty or tenant-occupied homes (estates, divorces); a reviewer may want the owner-present variant as the main story. Counsel question (also in pf.money): whether a rule against paying for appraisal assignments reaches Rosfield's $2.
